newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals ranged, traders await agency rates.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals ranged, traders await agency rates.

text.p: Tin prices suffered a fresh setback on the metal market on Thursday, dealers said.

Other base metals moved in a narrow range and finished on a quiet note. Volume was poor as major players kept to the sidelines awaiting the annoucement of the selling prices by state-owned agencies for November.
Meanwhile ready tin fell by 200 rupees to 35,300 rupees per quintal on higher supplies and fresh offerings by stockists, following a weak trend in the world market.
Copper was steady at 11,650 rupees per quintal as was lead at 4,800 rupees and nickel at 37,500 rupees per quintal.

On Wednesday copper and lead were down by 50 rupees while nickel was down by 100 rupees per quintal. Aluminium remained quiet at 7,200 rupees per quintal, and so did zinc at 6,250 rupees per quintal amid nominal trading.
